parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no traveller-facing criminalisation, no facility-access ban, and no documented border or document-mismatch friction; foreign documents govern identity and the land border is open. These are substantial positives. Against them, gender identity is absent from hate-crime and anti-discrimination law, the 2019 UPR acceptance has no implementing text, and trans-specific incident/enforcement data are absent. Legal gender recognition is missing but is resident-facing and does not directly expose visitors. LGB acceptance signals a climate unlikely to be actively hostile, but trans-specific social acceptance and recourse are undocumented. This sits below jurisdictions with documented GI protections and working remedies, but well above those with screening, detention, or facility exclusion.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border screening, marker-mismatch questioning, or entry refusal; the land border is open and foreign documents govern identity.
entry_documents.protection: No trans-specific entry restriction is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry does not trigger local gender-marker processes, and no checkpoint exposure is recorded.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented police stops, identity investigations, detention, or custody placement practice aimed at trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific custody or detention protocol is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Without documented stops or investigations, no chain from document mismatch to birth-sex custody is shown.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No statute regulates bathroom or facility use, and no exclusion of trans visitors is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The state is unitary; no subnational facility variation is documented.

care_services.exposure: No denial of care or medication to trans visitors is documented; absence of legal gender recognition affects residents.
care_services.interaction: Visitor documents are not reissued locally, but care access for trans visitors remains an open question.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No gender-identity criminalisation or state threat-framing is documented; hate-crime enhancement covers sexual orientation only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime provision is in force; UPR acceptance is unimplemented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The missing GI protection may limit recourse after bias crime, but no state hostility toward trans visitors is shown.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-dependent trans-specific rule is documented; a minor faces the same unregulated facilities and absence of GI protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's foreign documents govern; no school, enrolment, or visitor-specific exposure is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Occasional LGBTQ violence is reported without figures or a trans-specific pattern; police response is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No evidence shows such violence is state-tolerated or aimed at visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity-specific recourse is documented, and application of hate-crime enhancements is unpublished.
remedies_unknowns.protection: General courts exist, but no trans-visitor remedy is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: It is unresolved whether hotels, police, or officials reliably honour foreign markers.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a visitor register, routine exclusion, and no effective remedy. This jurisdiction has no documented entry screening, no exclusion practice, and an open land border, so it sits materially higher.

0.55-B documents extended secondary screening, document-divergence detention, and discretionary denial. Here no border screening or mismatch friction is recorded and foreign documents govern, placing this jurisdiction above 0.55-B despite thinner GI protections.

0.75-C documents trained border officers, an appeal tribunal, and working remedies after brief detention. This jurisdiction has no documented trans-specific border friction, but also no documented GI protection or remedy; it is comparable on absent severe exposure but slightly below on verified protection.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime presents no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility exclusion, no documented border friction, and an open land border with foreign documents controlling identity. Those facts keep the traveller out of the severe and high-risk tiers. The weakness is evidentiary and protective: gender identity is outside hate-crime and anti-discrimination law, UPR acceptance is unimplemented, and no trans-specific incidents, enforcement data, or remedies are recorded. Legal gender recognition is absent but resident-facing, not a visitor exposure. LGB-tolerant signals make state or social threat-framing unlikely, but trans-specific acceptance and recourse remain unverified, so the rating sits in the reduced-risk band below jurisdictions with documented GI protections.
